big-bang.title: The Big Bang
big-bang.hook: The heavens and the earth were “a joined entity” — and then they were split apart.
big-bang.science.0: Every distant galaxy is moving away from us, and the farther away it is, the faster it recedes. Run that film backwards and all matter, energy and space converge into a single hot, dense state. That is the Big Bang model: not an explosion in space, but the expansion of space itself, starting about 13.8 billion years ago.
big-bang.science.1: The evidence comes in layers. Galaxies recede (Hubble, 1929). A faint glow of microwaves fills the whole sky at 2.725 K, the afterglow of the early universe, found by accident in 1965 by Penzias and Wilson. And the mix of light elements in old gas clouds, about 75% hydrogen and 25% helium by mass, matches what the model predicts.
big-bang.science.2: In its youth the universe was an opaque, hot gas, a kind of cosmic “smoke”, that cooled and clumped into the first stars and galaxies. Verse 41:11 speaks of the heaven at a stage when it was “smoke” (dukhān).
big-bang.stats.0.label: Age of the universe (Planck 2018)
big-bang.stats.1.label: Temperature of the cosmic microwave background
big-bang.stats.2.label: Hydrogen / helium in the primordial gas
big-bang.proof.0.title: Lemaître: the universe must be expanding
big-bang.proof.0.text: The Belgian priest and physicist Georges Lemaître shows from Einstein's equations that the universe cannot be static, and estimates the rate of expansion from galaxy data. In 1931 he proposes it began as a single “primeval atom”.
big-bang.proof.1.title: Hubble: the farther, the faster
big-bang.proof.1.text: Edwin Hubble plots the speed of galaxies against their distance and finds a straight line. Run backwards, everything converges.
big-bang.proof.1.cap: Hubble's original 1929 plot: each dot is a galaxy, the farther away, the faster it recedes.
big-bang.proof.2.title: Alpher and Herman: a predicted afterglow
big-bang.proof.2.text: Ralph Alpher and Robert Herman calculate that a hot early universe would leave a faint microwave glow, a few kelvin above absolute zero.
big-bang.proof.3.title: Penzias and Wilson: they hear it
big-bang.proof.3.text: At Bell Labs, Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson cannot get rid of a faint hiss in their horn antenna, from every direction, day and night: the afterglow, about 3.5 K. Nobel Prize 1978.
big-bang.proof.3.cap: The Holmdel horn antenna where the afterglow of the Big Bang was found.
big-bang.proof.4.title: COBE, WMAP and Planck map it
big-bang.proof.4.text: Satellites measure the glow: a near-perfect 2.725 K with tiny ripples that grew into galaxies. Planck fixes the age of the universe at about 13.8 billion years.
big-bang.proof.4.cap: The afterglow of the early universe, mapped by ESA's Planck satellite.
big-bang.fit.0: One joined mass that was then separated matches a single hot, dense state that expanded and cooled.
big-bang.fit.1: 41:11 has the heaven as “smoke” before it took shape, matching the hot gas stage before the first stars.
big-bang.gap.0: No date, temperature or mechanism is given.
big-bang.gap.1: The Earth formed about 9 billion years after the Big Bang, so “the heavens and the earth” cannot mean our planet literally.
big-bang.gap.2: The Big Bang is the expansion of space, not an explosion into space; “split” is a picture, not physics.
big-bang.media.0.cap: Timeline of the universe, from the Big Bang to today (NASA/WMAP).
big-bang.media.1.cap: The afterglow of the early universe, mapped by ESA's Planck satellite.
big-bang.media.2.cap: Hubble Ultra Deep Field: thousands of galaxies in a patch of sky the size of a grain of sand.
big-bang.media.3.cap: How the early universe's glow became the cosmic microwave background.
big-bang.media.4.cap: Listen: physicist John Cramer turned the ripples in the afterglow into sound, raised about 100 septillion times in pitch so ears can hear it. A sonification, not a recording.
expanding-universe.title: The Expanding Universe
expanding-universe.hook: A verse about a heaven that is being expanded, 1,300 years before Hubble measured it.
expanding-universe.science.0: In 1929 Edwin Hubble showed that distant galaxies are receding, and the farther away, the faster they go. Georges Lemaître had predicted the same relation two years earlier from Einstein's equations. The cause is not galaxies flying through space: space itself is stretching.
expanding-universe.science.1: Today's rate is about 70 km/s for every megaparsec (3.26 million light-years) of distance. Different measurement methods disagree slightly, an open puzzle called the “Hubble tension”. In 1998 two teams discovered that the expansion is even accelerating, work that earned the 2011 Nobel Prize in Physics.
expanding-universe.stats.0.label: Hubble's measurement of galaxy recession
expanding-universe.stats.1.label: The Hubble constant
expanding-universe.stats.2.label: Accelerating expansion discovered
expanding-universe.proof.0.title: Slipher: galaxies are moving away
expanding-universe.proof.0.text: Vesto Slipher measures the light of spiral “nebulae” at Lowell Observatory and finds most shifted toward red: they are receding, some at over 1,000 km/s.
expanding-universe.proof.0.cap: The spectrograph used at Lowell Observatory to measure how fast the spirals move.
expanding-universe.proof.1.title: Lemaître: speed should grow with distance
expanding-universe.proof.1.text: Lemaître predicts from Einstein's equations that recession speed grows with distance, and calculates the rate from real data.
expanding-universe.proof.2.title: Hubble: the straight line
expanding-universe.proof.2.text: Hubble measures distances with Cepheid variable stars and confirms it: velocity rises in step with distance. His original plot is shown here.
expanding-universe.proof.3.title: Two teams: the expansion is speeding up
expanding-universe.proof.3.text: Teams led by Saul Perlmutter, and by Brian Schmidt and Adam Riess, find distant Type Ia supernovae fainter than expected. The expansion is accelerating. Nobel Prize 2011.
expanding-universe.proof.3.cap: Supernova 1994D, a Type Ia explosion in the galaxy NGC 4526. Exploding stars like this are “standard candles” used to measure the expansion.
expanding-universe.proof.4.title: The Hubble tension
expanding-universe.proof.4.text: Measurements from the early universe (Planck, about 67 km/s/Mpc) and from nearby supernovae (about 73) disagree by more than expected: an open puzzle.
expanding-universe.proof.4.cap: Different measurements of the Hubble constant (NOIRLab).
expanding-universe.fit.0: The verb form is continuing (“We are expanding it”), matching a universe that is still expanding.
expanding-universe.fit.1: The heaven is “constructed with strength” first and then expanded, matching a structured cosmos whose space stretches.
expanding-universe.gap.0: Some classical scholars read musiʿūn as “We have vast capacity”, not “expanders”.
expanding-universe.gap.1: The verse gives no rate, no acceleration and no mechanism.
expanding-universe.gap.2: In physics, space itself stretches; the word “expander” alone does not say that.
expanding-universe.media.0.cap: Hubble eXtreme Deep Field: galaxies that are still moving apart.
expanding-universe.media.1.cap: Artist's timeline of the expanding universe (NASA/WMAP).
expanding-universe.media.2.cap: NASA explains the Hubble constant and the expanding universe.
orbits.title: Everything Moves in an Orbit
orbits.hook: Sun, Moon, night and day: “each in an orbit, swimming.”
orbits.science.0: The Moon circles the Earth every 27.3 days at about 1 km/s. The Earth circles the Sun at about 30 km/s. The Sun itself circles the centre of the Milky Way. Nothing in the sky is nailed in place: every body follows a path set by gravity.
orbits.science.1: The verb yasbaḥūn is the one used for swimming: a body gliding freely along its own path, touching nothing. Verse 36:40 adds that the Sun cannot overtake the Moon, nor night outrun day: a picture of orderly cycles that never collide.
orbits.science.2: Kepler showed in 1609 that planetary orbits are ellipses, and Newton explained them with gravity in 1687. Verse 55:5 says the Sun and Moon move by “ḥusbān”, exact calculation, which is why eclipses can be predicted years in advance to within a few seconds.
orbits.stats.0.label: Moon's orbit around the Earth
orbits.stats.1.label: Earth's speed around the Sun
orbits.stats.2.label: Moon's speed around the Earth
orbits.proof.0.title: Copernicus: the Sun at the centre
orbits.proof.0.text: Nicolaus Copernicus puts the Sun near the centre and sets the planets moving around it.
orbits.proof.1.title: Kepler: ellipses, not circles
orbits.proof.1.text: Using Tycho Brahe's measurements of Mars, Johannes Kepler shows that planets follow ellipses and sweep equal areas in equal times.
orbits.proof.2.title: Newton: gravity explains the paths
orbits.proof.2.text: Isaac Newton shows that one force, gravity, explains falling apples, the Moon's orbit and the tides. Every orbit is a fall that keeps missing.
orbits.proof.3.title: Halley's comet returns
orbits.proof.3.text: Edmond Halley used Newton's laws to predict that a comet would return in 1758, long after his death. It did: the first proof that gravity governs comets too.
orbits.proof.3.cap: Halley's Comet crossing the Milky Way, 1986 (NASA).
orbits.proof.4.title: Neptune found by calculation
orbits.proof.4.text: Urbain Le Verrier calculated where an unseen planet must be from oddities in Uranus's orbit. Astronomers found Neptune within about one degree of his prediction on the first night.
orbits.fit.0: Everything named (Sun, Moon, night and day) is described as moving along its own path.
orbits.fit.1: Yasbaḥūn (glide freely) suits bodies moving through space without touching anything.
orbits.fit.2: 55:5 says the Sun and Moon move by exact calculation, matching eclipses that can be predicted years ahead.
orbits.gap.0: Falak in classical Arabic astronomy meant a sphere or course, not specifically an ellipse.
orbits.gap.1: The verse does not say what keeps the bodies on their paths (gravity).
orbits.gap.2: Ancient astronomers also knew the Sun, Moon and planets follow regular paths; the verse describes rather than reveals a hidden law.
orbits.media.0.cap: An illustration of the Solar System's bodies, each on its own orbit.
orbits.media.1.cap: NASA: the Moon's orbit around the Earth.
orbits.media.2.cap: ESO animation: bodies of the outer Solar System on their orbits.
sun-moving.title: The Sun Is Moving
sun-moving.hook: The Sun is not standing still. It runs a course of its own, and its planets travel with it.
sun-moving.science.0: For most of history the Sun was thought to be the fixed centre of the sky. In 1783 William Herschel showed from the motions of stars that the Sun itself is travelling through space. In the 1920s Bertil Lindblad and Jan Oort proved that the Milky Way rotates and that the Sun circles its centre.
sun-moving.science.1: Today we know the Sun moves at roughly 230 km/s (over 800,000 km/h) around the galactic centre, 26,000 light-years away, completing one lap about every 230 million years. In 2021 ESA's Gaia satellite even measured the tiny acceleration of the Solar System toward the centre: about 7 mm/s more every year.
sun-moving.science.2: The planets go along for the ride. They are bound to the Sun by gravity, so the whole Solar System travels as one, like passengers in a moving train. The verse itself speaks only of the Sun's run; that the planets travel with it is established science, not a phrase we put in the verse's mouth.
sun-moving.stats.0.label: Sun's speed around the Milky Way
sun-moving.stats.1.label: One lap of the galaxy (a “galactic year”)
sun-moving.stats.2.label: Distance to the galactic centre
sun-moving.proof.0.title: Halley: the “fixed stars” are not fixed
sun-moving.proof.0.text: Edmond Halley notices that Sirius, Arcturus and Aldebaran have shifted since the ancient Greeks charted them.
sun-moving.proof.1.title: Herschel: the Sun is travelling
sun-moving.proof.1.text: William Herschel analyses the motions of stars and concludes that the Sun itself is moving through space, toward the constellation Hercules.
sun-moving.proof.2.title: Shapley: the Sun is far from the centre
sun-moving.proof.2.text: Harlow Shapley maps the globular clusters of the Milky Way and shows that the Sun lies far from the galaxy's centre.
sun-moving.proof.3.title: Oort: the galaxy rotates
sun-moving.proof.3.text: Jan Oort shows that the stars of the Milky Way rotate around a distant centre, with the Sun among them.
sun-moving.proof.4.title: Gaia: the acceleration is measured
sun-moving.proof.4.text: ESA's Gaia satellite measures how the Solar System accelerates toward the galactic centre: about 7 mm/s more every year.
sun-moving.proof.4.cap: ESA/Gaia measures the Solar System's acceleration.
sun-moving.fit.0: The verse says the Sun runs (tajrī), a verb of motion, when many people took the Sun as the fixed centre of the sky.
sun-moving.fit.1: 21:33 says all the bodies, the Sun included, “swim” in their orbits.
sun-moving.gap.0: Mustaqarr is read as a resting place, a fixed course or an appointed end.
sun-moving.gap.1: The verse does not mention the galaxy or the planets travelling with the Sun.
sun-moving.gap.2: The Sun's apparent daily movement across the sky also fits the verse.

sun-moving.media.1.cap: Our galaxy, the Milky Way, over the Paranal Observatory (ESO).
sun-moving.media.2.cap: ESA/Gaia: nearby stars, the Sun among them, orbiting the galaxy.

sun-moon-light.title: A Burning Lamp and a Borrowed Light
sun-moon-light.hook: The Sun is a “lamp” that burns. The Moon is a “light” that shines by borrowed brilliance.
sun-moon-light.science.0: The Sun makes its own light. In its core, at about 15 million °C, roughly 600 million tonnes of hydrogen fuse into helium every second. Hans Bethe worked out the fusion cycles that power stars in 1938–39. The Sun literally burns: a nuclear lamp.
sun-moon-light.science.1: The Moon makes none. Its surface is dark rock that reflects only about 12% of the sunlight falling on it. Every glimmer of moonlight is the Sun's, borrowed.
sun-moon-light.science.2: The Quran uses different words for the two: sirāj (a burning lamp) and ḍiyāʾ (radiance) for the Sun, nūr and munīr for the Moon. Whether the distinction is deliberate is a matter of linguistic interpretation, but it is precise.
sun-moon-light.stats.0.label: Hydrogen fused in the Sun's core
sun-moon-light.stats.1.label: Temperature of the Sun's core
sun-moon-light.stats.2.label: Sunlight the Moon reflects
sun-moon-light.proof.0.title: Anaxagoras: the Moon borrows light
sun-moon-light.proof.0.text: The Greek philosopher Anaxagoras says the Moon shines by reflected sunlight. This was already known long before the Quran.
sun-moon-light.proof.1.title: Eddington: stars burn hydrogen
sun-moon-light.proof.1.text: Arthur Eddington argues that stars shine by fusing hydrogen into helium.
sun-moon-light.proof.2.title: Bethe: the Sun's reactions
sun-moon-light.proof.2.text: Hans Bethe works out the nuclear reactions that power the Sun. Nobel Prize 1967.
sun-moon-light.proof.3.title: Davis: neutrinos from the core
sun-moon-light.proof.3.text: Ray Davis catches neutrinos from the Sun's core in a tank of cleaning fluid deep underground: direct proof that fusion is burning there. Nobel Prize 2002.
sun-moon-light.proof.3.cap: A neutrino detector exhibit: the kind of instrument that sees the Sun's core.
sun-moon-light.fit.0: Different words are used: sirāj (a burning lamp) for the Sun and nūr (light) for the Moon.
sun-moon-light.fit.1: 10:5 calls the Sun's light ḍiyāʾ (radiance) and the Moon's nūr. Many Arabic lexicographers treat ḍiyāʾ as light that comes from a source itself.
sun-moon-light.gap.0: Greek astronomers already knew the Moon reflects sunlight.
sun-moon-light.gap.1: Nūr and ḍiyāʾ are also used loosely elsewhere, so the distinction is not absolute.
sun-moon-light.gap.2: The verse says nothing about nuclear fusion.
sun-moon-light.media.0.cap: The Sun, imaged by NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory.
sun-moon-light.media.1.cap: The Full Moon, lit entirely by the Sun.

protected-sky.title: The Protected Ceiling
protected-sky.hook: “We made the sky a protected ceiling”, and a thin layer of gas and magnetism really does guard life.
protected-sky.science.0: Earth's atmosphere is a shield. The ozone layer absorbs 97–99% of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet light. The air burns up the small rocks that hit it at 11 to 72 km/s, tens of tonnes of space debris every day, so almost none reaches the ground.
protected-sky.science.1: Higher up, Earth's magnetic field (the magnetosphere) deflects the charged particles of the solar wind. Where a few slip in near the poles, they glow as the aurora.
protected-sky.science.2: Without this double shield the surface would be sterilised by radiation. Mars, with almost no global magnetic field and a thin atmosphere, is the cold demonstration: it lost most of its early air.
protected-sky.stats.0.label: Harmful UV absorbed by the ozone layer
protected-sky.stats.1.label: Speed of meteoroids meeting the atmosphere
protected-sky.proof.0.title: Fabry and Buisson: the ozone layer
protected-sky.proof.0.text: Charles Fabry and Henri Buisson find that the Sun's ultraviolet is cut off sharply at short wavelengths: a layer of ozone high in the atmosphere is absorbing it.
protected-sky.proof.1.title: Explorer 1: belts of trapped radiation
protected-sky.proof.1.text: America's first satellite carries James Van Allen's radiation counter. It is overwhelmed in some regions: belts of charged particles trapped by Earth's magnetic field.
protected-sky.proof.2.title: Farman and colleagues: a hole in the shield
protected-sky.proof.2.text: British Antarctic Survey scientists Joe Farman, Brian Gardiner and Jonathan Shanklin report a huge loss of ozone over Antarctica, showing how much the shield matters. The Montreal Protocol follows in 1987.
protected-sky.proof.2.cap: The Antarctic ozone hole seen from space (NASA).
protected-sky.proof.3.title: MAVEN: a planet without a shield
protected-sky.proof.3.text: NASA's MAVEN orbiter measures Mars losing its atmosphere to the solar wind, showing what can happen to a planet without a strong magnetic shield.
protected-sky.proof.3.cap: Solar storm particles stripping Mars's atmosphere (NASA/MAVEN illustration).
protected-sky.fit.0: Two shields work overhead: the atmosphere absorbs harmful radiation and burns up meteoroids, and the magnetic field deflects charged particles.
protected-sky.fit.1: “Ceiling” (saqf) and “protected” (maḥfūẓ) fit a covering that guards those beneath it.
protected-sky.gap.0: Samāʾ can mean the sky, the atmosphere or the heavens in general.
protected-sky.gap.1: “Protected” has also been read as protected from falling or from devils; the radiation reading is modern.
protected-sky.gap.2: Older cultures also called the sky a canopy; ozone and the magnetosphere are not in the verse.

speed-of-light.title: The Speed of Light Puzzle
speed-of-light.hook: Can the speed of light be read out of a verse? Here is the calculation, and where it becomes contested.
speed-of-light.proofH: How the real speed of light was measured
speed-of-light.science.0: Verse 32:5 says that every matter “will ascend to Him in a Day, the extent of which is a thousand years of those which you count”. Verse 70:4 says the angels ascend in a Day “the extent of which is fifty thousand years”, and 22:47 says a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of your counting. Classical commentators read these as divine time, or as the Day of Judgment.
speed-of-light.science.1: A modern proposal by the Egyptian astronomer Mansour Hassab-Elnaby reads 32:5 as a distance–time statement: something covers in one day the distance the Moon covers in 12,000 lunar months (1,000 lunar years × 12). Try the arithmetic in the lab below.
speed-of-light.science.2: For reference, the speed of light is exactly 299,792.458 km/s, fixed by definition of the metre since 1983.
speed-of-light.stats.0.label: The speed of light
speed-of-light.stats.1.label: Lunar months in 1,000 lunar years
speed-of-light.stats.2.label: Raw result vs. the true speed of light
speed-of-light.proof.0.title: Rømer: light takes time
speed-of-light.proof.0.text: Ole Rømer times the eclipses of Jupiter's moon Io and finds them arriving late when the Earth is farther away. Light has a finite speed; he estimates about 220,000 km/s.
speed-of-light.proof.1.title: Fizeau: no astronomy needed
speed-of-light.proof.1.text: Hippolyte Fizeau sends a light beam through a spinning toothed wheel to a mirror several kilometres away and back, and measures about 315,000 km/s on Earth.
speed-of-light.proof.2.title: The metre is defined by light
speed-of-light.proof.2.text: The metre is redefined as the distance light travels in 1/299,792,458 of a second, so the speed of light is now exactly 299,792,458 m/s.
speed-of-light.fit.0: If every choice in the author's method is made, the answer lands within 0.001% of the true value.
speed-of-light.fit.1: The verses do link a “day” to “a thousand years”, so a ratio can be formed.
speed-of-light.gap.0: The verses never mention light, the Moon or a distance.
speed-of-light.gap.1: The number needs the Earth-motion correction, which critics say is chosen to make it fit.
speed-of-light.gap.2: 70:4 (50,000 years) gives 50 times the speed of light with the same recipe.
speed-of-light.gap.3: Classical commentators read these verses as divine time or the Day of Judgment, not physics.
speed-of-light.gap.4: A mathematician's review says the “distance the Moon travels” in this recipe has no natural physical meaning.
